title: TMX Flow
description: Schema for a TMX Flow document. A Flow is the static definition of an Environment, a Context and a list of Tasks. Only `tasks` is required. Environment and Context may be inlined as objects or referenced by path/name so they can be reused across Flows. Standalone artifact files (environment.*, context.*, task-N.*) validate against the corresponding sub-schemas under `$defs` (`environment`, `context`, `task`). This document targets YAML/JSON/JSONC/TOML sources after they are parsed to a JSON model.

flow.title: Flow
flow.description: A static definition of tasks, plus optional context and environment. At runtime an instance of a Flow is a Pipeline.

kind.description: Optional artifact discriminator. When present, a single validator can dispatch a file to the right schema instead of relying on filename convention. Defaults to `flow` for a top-level document.

version.description: Optional version/identifier for this Flow definition.

environment.description: Runtime environment for the Flow. Inline object, or a string path/name referencing a reusable environment definition. Optional — Flows run without one.

context.description: Context (env vars, secrets, lifecycle hooks) for the Flow. Inline object, or a string path/name referencing a reusable context definition.

inputs.description: Declared input variables the Flow accepts when invoked — from the CLI (`tmx run flow.yaml --input name=value`) or from a calling `flow` task's `inputs`. Each value is referenced inside the Flow as `${{ inputs.NAME }}`. Maps input name → input spec.

tasks.description: The tasks the Flow runs. Either an ordered array of tasks, or a name-keyed map (object) whose keys are task names. The array form is explicitly ordered — tasks run top to bottom. The map form runs in the source document's key order (the order properties appear in the YAML/JSON/JSONC/TOML file).

inputSpec.title: Input variable spec
inputSpec.description: Declaration of a single Flow input variable. A supplied value is referenced inside the Flow as `${{ inputs.NAME }}`.

type.description: Expected JSON type of the input value.

required.description: When true, the input must be supplied at invocation.

default.description: Value used when the input is not supplied. Any JSON type.

taskList.title: Task list
taskList.description: An ordered list of tasks. Tasks run in sequence, one after another. There is no branching, looping or parallel execution; a task may be skipped via its `if` condition.

tasks.title: Task collection
tasks.description: A set of tasks, expressed as EITHER an ordered array OR a name-keyed map. Array form (`taskList`): tasks run in the order they appear; each item is a full task object (no string shorthand). Map form: a JSON object whose property names are the task names and whose values are either a full task object (which need not repeat `name`) or a string shorthand for an `exec` task; tasks run in the source document's key order (the order keys appear in the YAML/JSON/JSONC/TOML file). Both forms run in sequence — there is no branching, looping or parallel execution.

oneOf.title: Task map
oneOf.description: A name-keyed map of tasks: each property name is the task's name and its value is either a task object or a string shorthand for an `exec` task (the string is run as a shell command). Runs in the source document's key order.
Shorthand for an exec task: the string is run as a shell command (equivalent to { type: 'exec', with: { command: <string> } }). The map key is the task name.

reference.title: Reference
reference.description: A string reference to a standalone artifact: a relative/absolute file path or a registered name.

task.title: Task
task.description: A single step in a Flow. Every task consumes the current Pipeline state (a JSON object) and returns a JSON output that is merged back into the Pipeline state for subsequent tasks. Non-JSON stdout is wrapped as `{ "message": "..." }`; binary output is wrapped as `{ "blob": <bytes> }`.

kind.description: Optional artifact discriminator for standalone task files (task-N.*). Lets a single validator dispatch by `kind` rather than filename.

name.description: Identifier for the task. Should be unique within the Flow. Task output is merged into the Pipeline state under this name (`state[name] = output`).

type.description: The task implementation to run. One of the built-in types, or `flow` to import another Flow as a user-defined task.

if.description: Skip condition: a JavaScript-subset expression evaluated against the Pipeline state, using JS truthy/falsy semantics and strict equality (===). When it evaluates falsy, the task is skipped. This is the only supported control flow.

secrets.description: Names of context secrets this task requires. Secrets are auto-masked in all output by default; only secrets named here are unmasked and made available to this task. A task that names no secrets receives none in clear text.

context.description: Task-level context overrides. Inline object or a reference. By default merged over the folder/Flow context (`contextStrategy: merge`).

contextStrategy.description: How the task-level context combines with the inherited Flow/folder context. `merge` (default) merges each section (`env`, `secrets`, `hooks`) independently at the key level; `replace` uses only the task-level context.

contextPrecedence.description: On a key collision during `merge`, which side wins. `local` (default) — the in-file/task value overrides the inherited value; `inherited` — the parent/folder value overrides the local value.

output.description: Optional override for the Pipeline-state key this task's output is merged under. Defaults to the task `name`.

continueOnError.description: When true, a failing task does not abort the Pipeline; the error is recorded and the next task runs.

with.description: Type-specific configuration. The accepted shape is determined by `type` (see the allOf branches).

args.description: Arguments passed to the command. When set, `command` is treated as the executable.

shell.description: Shell to run the command in, e.g. 'bash', 'sh', 'pwsh'. Implementation default when omitted.

runWith.title: Run task
runWith.description: Run a program/script in a named language/interpreter. Provide either inline `script` or a `file` path. Distinct from `exec`, which runs a single shell command line.

language.description: Interpreter/runtime, e.g. 'python', 'node', 'ruby', 'bash', 'deno'. Defaults to 'bash' when omitted.

file.description: Path to a script file to execute.

body.description: Request body. An object/array is serialised per `bodyType`.

fileWith.title: File task
fileWith.description: Read or write files on the local filesystem.

storeWith.title: Store task
storeWith.description: Read from or write to S3-compatible object storage.

key.description: Object key. Required for get/put/delete/head; used as a prefix for list.

endpoint.description: S3-compatible endpoint URL. Omit for AWS S3 defaults.

credentials.description: Access credentials. Values typically reference secrets from the context.

chatCompletionWith.title: Chat Completion task
chatCompletionWith.description: Call an LLM using the ChatCompletions API specification.

apiUrl.description: Full URL of the ChatCompletions API endpoint to call, e.g. 'https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions'.

apiKey.description: API key. Typically references a secret from the context.

responseFormat.description: Structured-output / response-format directive passed through to the API.

content.description: Message content. String, or an array of content parts for multimodal input.

assertWith.title: Assert / Expect task
assertWith.description: Assert values from the Pipeline state. The task fails if any assertion does not hold.

assertion.title: Assertion
assertion.description: A single assertion modelled on Vitest's `expect` API (https://vitest.dev/api/expect.html): `expect(actual).matcher(expected)`. Vitest's `.not` modifier (`expect(actual).not.matcher(...)`) maps to `not: true`. Only value matchers are supported; mock- and promise-only matchers (toHaveBeenCalled, resolves, rejects, …) are excluded as they do not apply to asserting plain values.

actual.description: The value or expression under test — typically a `${{ ... }}` reference resolved against the Pipeline state. Corresponds to the argument of `expect(actual)`.

matcher.description: The Vitest `expect` matcher to apply (see https://vitest.dev/api/expect.html). The assertion holds when `expect(actual).matcher(expected)` passes; the `.not` modifier is expressed via `not: true`.

not.description: Negate the matcher, mirroring Vitest's `.not` modifier (`expect(actual).not.matcher(...)`). When true, the assertion holds when the matcher would otherwise fail.

expected.description: Argument passed to the matcher. Omitted for unary matchers (`toBeTruthy`, `toBeFalsy`, `toBeNull`, `toBeUndefined`, `toBeDefined`, `toBeNaN`). For matchers that take multiple arguments (e.g. `toHaveProperty(path, value)`, `toBeCloseTo(number, precision)`), supply an array of those arguments. Any JSON type.

message.description: Custom failure message reported when the assertion does not hold.

flowWith.title: Flow (user-defined) task
flowWith.description: Import another Flow and run it as a single discrete task. This is how user-defined tasks are implemented.

inputs.description: Input variables passed into the imported Flow, keyed by the input names it declares (`inputs.NAME`). Available inside the imported Flow as `${{ inputs.NAME }}`.

context.title: Context
context.description: The environment variables, secrets and lifecycle hooks available to the tasks in a Flow. Contexts are reusable and may be defined standalone (context.*) for reuse across Flows.

kind.description: Optional artifact discriminator for standalone context files (context.*).

secrets.description: Named secrets available to tasks. A value is either a literal/interpolated string or a structured source descriptor. Secrets are auto-masked in all output; a task only receives the secrets it names in its `secrets` list.

hooks.description: Lifecycle hooks run over the course of a Pipeline.

change.description: Run every time the Pipeline state changes.

error.description: Run to handle errors in the Pipeline.

hook.title: Lifecycle hook
hook.description: A hook body: an inline set of tasks (an ordered array, or a name-keyed map where the key is the task name), or a reference to another Flow that implements the hook. The array form is explicitly ordered; the map form runs in the source document's key order.

inputs.description: Input variables passed into the referenced Flow, keyed by the input names it declares.

environment.title: Environment
environment.description: Declarative description of the runtime environment a Flow runs in. Used by an Environment Provider to provision resources for a Pipeline. Reusable and may be defined standalone (environment.*). Provider-specific keys are permitted at the top level and under `options`.

kind.description: Optional artifact discriminator for standalone environment files (environment.*).

platform.description: Target platform the environment runs on: local machine or a cloud provider.

provider.description: Name of the Environment Provider that materialises this environment. A provider is a standalone binary or a Flow implementing the bootstrap/deploy/clean/destroy methods. Defaults to a provider inferred from `platform`.

image.description: Standard image to use — a container image reference or a machine/VM image id.

bootstrap.description: Tasks to run on environment/container init. Follows the Flow task model — an inline set of tasks (an ordered array, or a name-keyed map where the key is the task name) or a reference to a Flow file. The array form is explicitly ordered; the map form runs in the source document's key order.

options.description: Provider/platform-specific options. The accepted shape is unique to each provider (e.g. AWS ECS differs from AWS EC2, fly.io, Google Cloud Run).

cpu.description: vCPU count or quantity, e.g. 2 or '500m'.

envMap.title: Environment variable map
envMap.description: Map of environment variable names to string values. Values may interpolate secrets or Pipeline state via the engine's ${{ ... }} syntax.

secretSource.title: Secret source
secretSource.description: Structured descriptor for where a secret value is read from. Provider-specific keys are permitted.

env.description: Read from a host environment variable.

duration.title: Duration
duration.description: A duration, either an integer number of seconds or a string like '500ms', '30s', '5m', '1h'.
